overview.summary: The canary_pyt extension provides the reference Python-based job definition format for Canary, commonly written as .pyt files.

minimal_pattern: Place canary_pyt or canary directives at module scope.
Place executable test logic in functions.
Read the running job (its parameters, name, working directory) from canary.get_instance(), a read-only snapshot. canary.get_job() is for extensions and hooks, not test bodies.
Exit with 0 for success or raise/use Canary failure helpers for structured outcomes.

lifecycle.summary: A .pyt file may declare a per-file setup and/or teardown function via bare decorators. They run in the worker process that executes the job, wrapping the test body.

decorators.canary_pyt.directives.setup: Registers a per-file setup function. Runs before the test body via the canary_runteststart hook. If it raises, the job is marked broken and the body does not run. One per file.
decorators.canary_pyt.directives.teardown: Registers a per-file teardown function. Runs after the test body via the canary_runtest_finish hook, regardless of the body's outcome. One per file.

behavior: During scanning the decorator records the function name onto the job spec attributes (__setup_fn__ / __teardown_fn__); at run time it is an identity decorator so the function stays defined.
At run time canary_pyt imports the job's .pyt in-process and calls the recorded function with the live canary.Job as its sole argument, inside the job workspace.
Setup/teardown are not separate jobs; they wrap the single test's execution.

directives.summary: Directives are generation-time declarations captured by the .pyt loader and converted into JobSpecIR objects.

common.testname: Set one or more generated test families.
common.name: Alias for testname.
common.parameterize: Generate job variants from parameter values.
common.cpus: Set fixed CPU requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.gpus: Set fixed GPU requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.nodes: Set fixed node requirement without creating a named parameter variant.
common.depends_on: Declare dependencies by name, pattern, or DependencySelector-like dictionary.
common.copy: Copy source files or directories into the job workspace.
common.link: Symlink source files or directories into the job workspace.
common.sources: Declare source files without staging them.
common.exclusive: Prevent concurrent execution with other jobs.
common.load_module: Load an environment module before execution.
common.source: Source an rc file before execution.
common.set_id: Set a stable explicit ID or ID template.
common.setup: Decorator registering a per-file setup function; runs before the test body (via canary_runteststart) with the live Job. One per file.
common.teardown: Decorator registering a per-file teardown function; runs after the test body (via canary_runtest_finish) with the live Job, regardless of outcome. One per file.
common.enable: Enable or disable generated jobs conditionally.
common.skipif: Skip jobs conditionally with a reason.
common.aggregate: Add one job that depends on all of this file's parameterized jobs and reruns the file with flag (or runs script); see ext.pyt.dependencies.depends_on_or_aggregate.

directives.when: Most directives take when=...: an expression over testname, platforms, options and parameters, as a string (when="platforms='not darwin'") or a dict (when={'parameters': 'breakfast=spam', 'options': 'extended'}). ext.pyt docs: conditional activation.

signatures.keywords: keywords(*args: str, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.timeout: timeout(arg: str | float | int, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.parameterize: parameterize(names: str | Sequence[str], values: Sequence[Sequence[Any] | Any], *, when: WhenType | None = None, type: enums.enums = enums.list_parameter_space, samples: int = 10, random_seed: float = 1234.0)
signatures.cpus: cpus(arg: int, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.gpus: gpus(arg: int, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.nodes: nodes(arg: int, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.depends_on: depends_on(*arg: DependencyType, when: WhenType | None = None, **kwargs)
signatures.copy: copy(*files: str, src: str | None = None, dst: str | None = None, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.link: link(*files: str, src: str | None = None, dst: str | None = None, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.sources: sources(*args: str, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.artifact: artifact(file: str, *, when: WhenType | None = None, save_on: str = 'always')
signatures.baseline: baseline(*, src: str | None = None, dst: str | None = None, when: WhenType | None = None, flag: str | None = None)
signatures.load_module: load_module(name: str, *, use: str | None = None, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.source: source(name: str, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.set_id: set_id(id: str, *, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.set_attribute: set_attribute(*, when: WhenType | None = None, **attributes: Any)
signatures.enable: enable(*args: bool, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.xfail: xfail(*, code: int = -1, when: WhenType | None = None)
signatures.aggregate: aggregate(*, when: WhenType | None = None, flag: str | None = None, script: str | None = None)

depends_on: canary_pyt.directives.depends_on('solve.n=*')                 # a pattern, matched after parameter expansion
copy: canary_pyt.directives.copy('input.yaml', 'mesh.exo')          # into the job's working directory

parameters.summary: parameterize() creates named job variants. cpus(), gpus(), and nodes() set fixed resource requirements without changing the generated display name.
common_mistakes: Using cpus() when named variants such as cpus=8 are desired; use parameterize('cpus', ...) instead.
Duplicating a key between parameters and meta_parameters.
Expecting top-level runtime code to be ignored during scan unless it is guarded.
Reading parameters from canary.get_job(); use canary.get_instance().parameters.
parameters.runtime_access: In the test body, canary.get_instance().parameters holds this job's values (item or attribute access: p['a'], p.a). Resource parameters (cpus, gpus, nodes) are included when set.

dependencies.summary: depends_on() supports strings, dictionaries, lists, and DependencySelector objects.

dictionary_keys.when: Dependency condition such as on_success, on_failure, always, or an outcome expression.
dictionary_keys.expects: Expected match count: '+', '?', '*', or a positive integer.

dependencies.patterns: A pattern matches job names after parameter expansion: 'solve.n=*' matches solve.n=10, solve.n=20, ...
dependencies.runtime_access: In the test body, canary.get_instance().dependencies holds a read-only snapshot of each upstream job: name, id, parameters, working_directory (where its files are), status (.category: PASS, FAIL, ...), keywords, timeout and its own dependencies. Read an upstream job's outputs from os.path.join(dep.working_directory, NAME).
dependencies.depends_on_or_aggregate: depends_on(...) makes this file's jobs depend on jobs from any file, chosen by name pattern, with when (on_success, always, ...) and expects (a count). aggregate(flag='--analyze') (aliases analyze, generate_composite_base_case) adds one job to this file, named after it, that depends on all of the file's parameterized jobs and reruns the file with the flag (or runs script=...); its parameters hold each parameter's values across the jobs as a tuple (n == (10, 20, 40)): one entry per job, duplicates included, entry i belonging to dependencies[i]. Use aggregate for one file's sweep, depends_on to join files.
example: # convergence.pyt: runs after every solve.n=* job passed
